extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, researchers, and policymakers interested in misinformation and media literacy
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and heuristics for recognizing and assessing websites that deliberately publish hoaxes, propaganda, or disinformation presented as real news, including technical, editorial, and behavioral signals. Useful for media literacy, fact-checking, and platform moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate publication of hoaxes/propaganda/disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Websites that deliberately publish fake news — hoaxes, propaganda, and disinformation purporting to be real news — often using social media to drive web traffic and amplify their effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sites intentionally seek to deceive readers rather than entertain (unlike satire). They commonly aim for financial or political gain and use social platforms to amplify reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent to be perceived as legitimate (vs satire)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike news satire, these websites deliberately seek to be perceived as legitimate and taken at face value, often for financial or political gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a site's presentation and behavior indicate it wants to pass as a mainstream outlet (no clear satirical disclaimer, imitation of established brands), treat it as potentially fraudulent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetization via digital advertising/programmatic ad trading
rubrics_metrics.description: Fake news websites monetize their content by exploiting the vulnerabilities of programmatic ad trading, a type of online advertising in which ads are traded through machine-to-machine auction in a real-time bidding system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for excessive ad placements, connections to ad networks known to serve such sites, and domain-hopping patterns intended to evade advertising blacklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impostor/spoofed site indicators (spoofed URLs, typosquatting, imitating layout)
rubrics_metrics.description: Impostor sites that appear to be legitimate news sites, newspapers, television stations or radio stations, often using spoofed URLs, typosquatting or otherwise imitating the layout and graphics of established news sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the domain closely (extra letters, different TLDs), compare logos and layout with the genuine outlet, and verify through official domain lists and publisher pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impersonation of defunct news sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Impersonating defunct news sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fraudulent actors may revive defunct outlet names to give stories apparent legacy credibility; verify existence and current ownership of the outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence/absence of a clear disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclaimer stating that its content is fictitious (especially on satire sites), or alternatively, no disclaimer at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire sites will often (but not always visibly) disclaim fictional content; the absence of a disclaimer on content that appears fictional is a red flag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Little to no contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Little to no contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legitimate news organizations provide clear contact and press office information; anonymity or hidden contacts suggest lower accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Little to no information about mission/staff/location
rubrics_metrics.description: Little to no information about the source's 'mission, staff members or physical location'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify 'About' pages and staff bios — vague or missing information suggests inauthenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site name changes after corrections by fact-checkers
rubrics_metrics.description: A site name that has been changed after being repeatedly corrected by fact-checking organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated name changes following debunking indicate evasive behavior and a pattern of misleading presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear classification (state-controlled/private_blog/satire)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'A state-controlled site, a private blog or ... a site containing satirical content' — unclear or misleading classification of the site's nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary when the site's proclaimed category conflicts with content; state-controlled or opaque ownership structures warrant extra scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: No disclosure of editorial responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: No disclosure of editorial responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of an editorial chain-of-responsibility (editors, corrections policy) is a sign of low accountability and potential disinformation intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: No legal notice for commercial offers
rubrics_metrics.description: No 'legal notice for any commercial offer'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legitimate commercial offers and sponsored content should carry legal notices; their absence may indicate deceptive commercial practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obscure or proxy domain registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Obscure or private website registration, such as using a proxy service to purchase the domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WHOIS privacy/proxy and incoherent registration info can hide ownership; cross-check registration history and related domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fabricated or incoherent domain registration metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabricated or incoherent domain registration metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inconsistent registration metadata (bogus addresses, mismatched owner info) is commonly used to conceal operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Established in a news desert / low local news coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Established in a news desert or otherwise has low local news coverage due to mass layoffs of journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites claiming to serve underserved regions may exploit news deserts to fill credibility gaps; verify local reporting capacity and presence of independent local outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing true and false content
rubrics_metrics.description: The site includes both true and false content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing some accurate material alongside falsehoods can increase perceived credibility; fact-check individual claims rather than assuming overall reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clickbait headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Clickbait headlines, with further signs of content with questionable veracity in the article text itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensational, emotionally-loaded headlines designed to drive clicks are a common tactic; open articles and check claims and sourcing before sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fictitious author bylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Fictitious author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify authorship (author profiles, other publications); invented bylines are a strong signal of fabrication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recycled photos used with different author/website
rubrics_metrics.description: Recycled photo in a different website by a different author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reverse-image-search photos to see if they are reused or misattributed; recycled imagery often signals fabrication or miscontextualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: No byline at all
rubrics_metrics.description: No byline at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of bylines reduces accountability; reputable outlets attribute reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors with reputations for spreading false information
rubrics_metrics.description: The author may have a reputation for spreading false information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check author histories and fact-check archives; patterns of false reporting indicate unreliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors who normally cover other topics
rubrics_metrics.description: A real claimed author, but who typically writes about a different topic than in the given article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sudden topical departure may indicate content spun or republished without legitimate expertise; corroborate claims with additional sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hidden byline
rubrics_metrics.description: Hidden byline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors listed only in sources not visible to readers (hidden/obscured attribution) is a tactic to avoid accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing sources that do not support the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The article cites sources that do not support the claim(s) made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check cited sources; mismatches between claim and citation often indicate deliberate misleading or poor scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations abbreviated or taken out of context
rubrics_metrics.description: For example, 'quotes are abbreviated or taken out of context'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locate original quotes to ensure they are not misrepresented; out-of-context quotes can change the meaning dramatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing fictitious sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The article cites sources that are fictitious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that named sources and outlets exist and are credible; fabricated sourcing is a direct sign of fabrication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fabricated quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: The article fabricates quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for primary-source transcripts, recordings, or credible reporting that reproduces the quote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims not covered by credible sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The article makes a claim that is not covered in credible sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extraordinary claims without independent corroboration should be treated skeptically and verified with established outlets or primary documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: False or out-of-context statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: The article contains false or out-of-context statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify statistical claims with original data sources and context; misused statistics are a common manipulation tactic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reposting from satire/impostor sites without clear attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The article is a repost of a story from another site (typically a satire/parody or impostor site), 'with or without attribution' and often 'omitting indications the [story is] made up'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace story origin; if a piece originated as satire or on an impostor domain, republication without clear labeling is deceptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Out-of-context or fabricated images
rubrics_metrics.description: The article contains out-of-context images or fabricated images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reverse-image search to check provenance and manipulation; altered or miscaptioned images are frequent deception tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cites unreliable/questionable sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The article cites unreliable or questionable sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess sources for credibility (peer review, established editorial standards); reliance on fringe or anonymous sources reduces trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copying content from established outlets without attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The article copies content from established news outlets without proper attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect plagiarism by comparing with original reporting; unattributed copying is a sign of bad faith or laziness in deceptive networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of large language models in content generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of large language models to generate content, sometimes evidenced by the inclusion of text prompts, LLM output phrases and/or hallucinations in the articles themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for tell-tale LLM artifacts (repetitive phrasing, fabricated citations, prompt text). AI-generated content may increase scale of disinformation and can contain hallucinated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline manipulation / recycled datetimes
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking a true news story out of context, for example, by reposting a story about an older event and claiming that it is directly related to an event happening currently; reposting a story from a credible source with a different header and publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check publication dates and original reporting to ensure events are not being misrepresented as recent or causally linked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting psychological biases / confirmation bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories are written to fit a target audience's confirmation biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious of stories that neatly confirm pre-existing beliefs for a particular group; such tailoring increases viral spread among sympathetic audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional appeals and psychological triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories contain content that appeals to emotions or is meant to stimulate psychological triggers, including anger and even violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-emotion content is designed to elicit shares and reduce critical thinking; verify facts before reacting or sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misspellings and sensational wording
rubrics_metrics.description: The story contains misspellings or 'sensational wording'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent typos and sensationalized prose often indicate low editorial standards and can be a heuristic for unreliable content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article spinning
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of article spinning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spun content may reuse the same base material to produce many superficially distinct articles; check for near-duplicate structures and phrasing across sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incoherent or unrealistic claims/images
rubrics_metrics.description: The story contains incoherent or unrealistic claims or images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess plausibility and corroborating evidence; implausible claims that lack independent verification are suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of evidence to support claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of evidence to support given claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credible reporting cites sources and documents; statements without evidence should be treated skeptically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of scams
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of scams within the site/content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify pay-to-access schemes, bogus offers, or requests for money/personal data; scams often co-occur with disinformation sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dubious or unprofessional website layout
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'dubious' or 'unprofessional-looking' layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poor design, broken links, and amateurish formatting can indicate low-quality or malicious sites, though not definitive on their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Excessive advertising', especially from services such as Content.ad, RevContent.com, or AdStyle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High ad density and certain ad networks are correlated with monetization-first fake-news sites; excessive ads can also indicate low editorial investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website logo created by text-to-image model
rubrics_metrics.description: Website logo created by text-to-image model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI-generated logos or low-quality branding may indicate recently created or deceptive outlets; cross-check with established brand registries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of malware / crypto-mining scripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of malware (including scripts for cryptocurrency mining).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical scans and browser warnings can reveal malicious scripts; malware presence is a strong indicator of malicious intent beyond misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding by biased actors
rubrics_metrics.description: Content [is] paid for by a company or politician or other potentially biased source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about funding or sponsorship should be visible; covertly funded political or corporate content is a conflict-of-interest risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete or obscured funding/sponsorship disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Incomplete or obscured disclaimer on funding or sponsorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of clear sponsorship disclosure reduces ability to assess bias; require funding transparency for credible evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared tracking/analytic/ad accounts linking sites (Google Analytics)
rubrics_metrics.description: They share the same Google Analytics account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shared analytics IDs are strong technical signals of a common operator or network; check page source for tracking IDs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared ad accounts linking sites (Google AdSense)
rubrics_metrics.description: They share the same Google AdSense account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common AdSense IDs indicate monetization-by-same-operator; useful for network attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared IP addresses among sites
rubrics_metrics.description: They share the same IP address(es).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-hosting or same-server use can indicate related sites; correlate with WHOIS/hosting providers for attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared Gravatar ID
rubrics_metrics.description: They share the same Gravatar ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shared Gravatar or profile identifiers can tie multiple domains to the same operator or authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared New Relic ID
rubrics_metrics.description: They share the same New Relic ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New Relic IDs embedded in pages can reveal operational linkages between domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared Quantcast or Matomo IDs
rubrics_metrics.description: They share the same Quantcast ID / They share the same Matomo ID Tracker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common audience/analytics trackers across domains are reliable network signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link spam between networked domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Link spam: They refer to each other's domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutual linking networks can amplify SEO and apparent credibility; check for reciprocal links among suspicious domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing identical or near-identical content across domains
rubrics_metrics.description: They publish the exact or near-exact same content, especially content that has been plagiarized from other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Near-duplicate content across domains is indicative of networked operations or content farming; use similarity detection to find clusters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared designs and metadata across sites
rubrics_metrics.description: They have the same or similar designs (layouts, bylines, privacy policies, 'About' pages, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template reuse suggests centralized production; compare HTML structure and asset usage for patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same owner(s) or hosting provider (domain registration evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: They have the same owner(s) or hosting provider, based on domain registration information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WHOIS and hosting records can connect domains to a single operator; look for recurring registrant names, emails, or hosts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain hopping to evade blacklists
rubrics_metrics.description: They use a technique called 'domain hopping' - repeatedly switching domain names to stay ahead of advertising blacklists on social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent domain changes with similar content/IDs suggest deliberate evasion; track historical domain registrations and redirects.
